Fed's Waller calls for more aggressive action to break psychology that 3% inflation is the norm
body: Fed Governor Waller is becoming increasingly concerned about the US inflation outlook, warning that price pressures are broadening beyond energy and that the Fed risks allowing higher inflation to become entrenched in consumers' and businesses' expectations.
Waller argues that the central bank needs to take a more aggressive action to convince markets and the public that it remains committed to bringing inflation back to its 2% target.

He highlighted that roughly 70% of components in the core services basket are currently experiencing inflation above 3%, suggesting that price pressures are no longer concentrated in energy-related categories.
He is concerned that businesses are becoming comfortable passing higher prices on to consumers, partly because they believe consumers remain resilient enough to absorb those increases.

If businesses expect to raise prices and consumers increasingly accept 3% inflation as normal, inflation expectations could become more entrenched, making it harder for the Fed to bring inflation back down, without a more aggressive tightening.

He thinks the Fed needs to break the psychology that inflation around 3% has become the new norm after failing to bring it back to the 2% target since 2021. He stressed that the Fed needs to become more aggressive, either by delivering a 50 bps rate hike or use monetary policy communications to signal a significantly tougher stance in the months ahead.

Simply maintaining the current policy trajectory might not be enough to change inflation expectations. The Fed needs to convince businesses, consumers and financial markets that it is prepared to take stronger action to restore price stability. He even suggested that the central bank might need to go beyond reversing the rate cuts implemented last year to bring inflation under control.

He also argued that the Fed should use statements, press conferences and forward guidance to steer market expectations towards a more restrictive policy outlook. A hawkish communication strategy could push interest rate expectations higher and tightening financial conditions enough to weigh on economic activity and inflation.

He also questioned the usefulness of the December Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), arguing that year-end projections might not adequately capture the evolving inflation picture. He prefers adopting a more forceful and forward-looking communication strategy rather than relying too heavily on projections that could quickly become outdated.

For now, Waller remains the only governor suggesting a more aggressive action, with the majority of Fed members preferring to move in small steps. Nevertheless, he's been a very influential member and his views have always preceded a change in monetary policy since 2021.
In the current context, traders should be very careful buying risk assets unless the Iran war ends or the Fed turns surprisingly dovish.

news.title: Zcash extends recovery but significant headwinds persist amid hawkish Fed and US-Iran tensions
body: Zcash has been recovering some losses after facing significant selling pressure over the past week, as hawkish Fed repricing and escalating US-Iran tensions triggered a broad wave of liquidations across the crypto market.

The fundamental picture remains net negative, with the US-Iran stalemate continuing to weigh on risk sentiment and Iran hardening its stance following the Republicans' losses in the US midterm elections. Meanwhile, Fed commentary remains hawkish amid elevated inflation concerns and persistent upside risks.
This combination has supported the US dollar and Treasury yields, tightening financial conditions and putting further pressure on risk assets, especially cryptocurrencies.

Looking ahead, Zcash will likely remain under pressure as long as the negative macro backdrop persists. A more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations will likely be needed to turn the risk sentiment around and reverse the bearish trend.

On the daily chart, we can see that Zcash has recovered some losses but the bearish trend remains intact amid the macro headwinds. If we get another selloff, we can expect the buyers to step in around the upward trendline, with a defined risk below it, to position for a rally into the downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking lower to increase the bearish bets into the 500.00 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor upward trendline defining the recovery. If we get a pullback, we can expect the buyers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep targeting the major downward trendline. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for break lower to increase the bearish bets into new lows.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the buyers will have a better risk to reward setup around the upward trendline, while the sellers will need a break to extend the drop into new lows. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we have the FOMC meeting minutes. Tomorrow, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on Fed speakers and the US-Iran developments.

news.title: Bitcoin remains under pressure amid the negative risk sentiment caused by hawkish Fed and US-Iran tensions
body: Bitcoin has been consolidating around recent lows after facing a big wave of liquidations over the past week due to the hawkish Fed repricing and increased US-Iran tensions.

The fundamental picture hasn’t changed as the US-Iran stalemate continues to drag on, with Iran hardening their stance after the Republicans loss at the US midterm elections. Meanwhile the Fed commentary continues to be hawkish amid elevated inflation and persistent risks.
This mix have been supporting the US dollar and Treasury yields, while weighing on risk assets amid increased growth concerns.
Looking ahead, Bitcoin will likely remain under pressure amid the negative macro backdrop. We will likely need a more dovish Fed or a breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations to reverse the trend.

On the daily chart, we can see that Bitcoin is consolidating around recent lows. If we get a pullback into the 67,000 resistance, we can expect the sellers to step in, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the 58,000 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the major downward trendline around the 75,000 level.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. If we get a pullback into the trendline, we can expect the sellers to lean on it, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break higher to increase the bullish bets into the major downward trendline next.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here given the choppy price action amid the consolidation. From a risk management perspective, the sellers will have a better risk to reward setup around the 67,000 resistance with a defined risk above the trendline. The buyers, on the other hand, will need a break above the trendline to open the door for new highs. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

news.title: Gold analysis shows we may be in an interesting potential bottom zone
body: Gold buyers are finally showing some resistance after an extended decline. Improving price action near $3,766 and a recovery toward $3,780 offer encouraging clues, but a sustained move toward $3,800 may be needed before the recovery becomes more convincing.

Gold futures are beginning to show something that has been missing during much of their recent decline: selling pressure is no longer consistently producing lasting lower prices. Buyers have made some encouraging progress, but there is still a substantial difference between identifying a possible bottom and confirming a bullish reversal.
The latest intraday evidence provides a practical framework for evaluating that difference.

Market snapshot: November 18, 2026, approximately 4:29 a.m. US Eastern time. Analysis based on December 2026 Micro Gold futures (MGC), with gold near $3,780.60. All prices below refer to that observation, not continuously updated quotations.
Gold recovered from an observed intraday low near $3,759.50, climbing back into an important area where much of the session's trading activity had previously taken place.
The lower boundary of that developing value area was around $3,766.20.

For readers unfamiliar with volume-based analysis, a value area represents a range where a substantial portion of trading volume has occurred. Its boundaries can help traders assess whether the market is accepting or rejecting a particular price region.
Gold initially moved back above that boundary, briefly slipped beneath it again, and subsequently recovered.
What makes the sequence interesting is that buyers did not surrender all their progress during subsequent pullbacks.
Instead, the shorter-term price structure began retaining higher prices.
The recovery eventually extended toward $3,780, accompanied by improving buying participation and upward price progress.
This suggests sellers may be losing some of their earlier effectiveness.
However, stronger buying in a short-term recovery does not automatically mean the broader bearish trend has ended.
These are reference levels, not automatic buy or sell instructions. VWAP, its deviation bands and the developing value area can move as trading continues.

news.title: Gold extends losses as strong US dollar and elevated yields hurt. What could change the trend?
body: Gold extended the selloff in the APAC session, although there was no catalyst for the move. The market just continues to move lower due to strong headwinds coming from higher Treasury yields and stronger US dollar after the hawkish repricing triggered by Fed commentary and the hotter than expected US CPI data.

For now, the bearish momentum remains strong, and we haven’t got any bullish catalyst to reverse the trend. Nevertheless, the hawkish repricing should now be mostly over, as a rate hike in December is widely expected, while the probability of a 50 bps hike remains very slim given that the majority of Fed members favour smaller steps.

Moreover, it looks like growth concerns are finally gaining traction, with the stock market trading around last week’s lows and Treasury yields slowly rolling over. These concerns are likely to persist and might even intensify as long as the US-Iran situation remains unresolved, and the Fed maintains the hawkish stance.

I think that in the current context, a prolonged US-Iran stalemate or an escalation would keep inflation expectations high alongside a weakening growth outlook, creating stagflationary expectations. And this should ultimately be bullish for gold. At the same time, if there’s a breakthrough, we could see a dovish repricing on easing inflation concerns, which should also support gold in the short-term.

There are certainly strong headwinds for gold at the moment, so these fundamental views will need to be paired with technicals for a confirmation of a change in momentum. If the stock market continues to fall, growth concerns could take centre stage and I would expect Treasury yields and the US dollar to weaken as well, supporting the precious metal.

On the daily chart, we can see that gold (CFD contract) extended the losses after a brief consolidation below the key 3,885 level. The natural target for the sellers should be the 3,500 level. If the price gets there, we can expect the buyers to step in, with a defined risk below the level, to position for a rally into the 4,700 level. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break to increase the bearish bets into the 3,100 level next.

On the 4 hour chart, we now have a downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. If we get a pullback, we can expect the sellers to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep targeting the 3,500 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to pile in for a rally into the 4,150 level next.

On the 1 hour chart, we have a minor downward trendline defining the bearish momentum on this timeframe. The sellers will likely lean on the trendline, with a defined risk above it, to keep pushing into new lows. The buyers, on the other hand, will look for a break to extend the pullback into the major trendline. The red lines define the average daily range for today.
Today we have the FOMC meeting minutes. Tomorrow, we get the latest US Jobless Claims figures. The focus will remain on Fed speakers and the US-Iran developments.

news.title: Record diesel prices drive UK inflation to 1-year high of 3.6%
body: U.K. inflation rose to 3.6% in the 12 months to October, its highest level in a year, as fuel costs continued to rise.
The reading was in line with the expectations of economists polled by Reuters and marked an increase from September's print of 3.5%.

Britain's Office for National Statistics said the largest contributor to the rising inflation rate was motor fuel costs, which rose 33.2% year-on-year. It was the largest one-year rise in motor fuel prices since July 2022, when energy costs surged in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The U.K. is a net energy importer, making it vulnerable to external energy shocks such as the one sparked by the disruption of trade through the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices have retreated from their wartime highs of well above $100 a barrel, but remain elevated.

The ONS said Wednesday that the average price of petrol rose by 5.2 pence (7 cents) per liter between September and October this year, compared with a 0.7 pence per liter rise in the same period a year earlier. The average petrol price stood at 174.7 pence per liter in October, the highest it's been since Aug. 2022.
Diesel prices rose by 7 pence per liter in October, with the average price reaching 199.5 pence per liter — the highest since ONS records began in 1996.
Since the U.S.-Iran war began in late February, inflation has risen sharply after a brief dip thanks to an energy price cap that was revised upward in July.

news.title: UK October CPI +3.6% vs +3.6% y/y expected
body: The market is focusing on the miss in services inflation and the unchanged core reading. The main upward pressure came from transport costs, particularly motor fuels, which made the largest positive contribution to the change in headline inflation. Restaurants and hotels provided the largest offsetting downward contribution.

The composition of inflation still warrants some caution, though. Goods inflation continued to accelerate, with the CPI goods annual rate rising from 3.2% to 3.5%. Services inflation, which is important for assessing domestic price pressures, remained relatively contained.

Overall, the data will be welcomed by the Bank of England as stable core and services inflation provide some reassurance that underlying price pressures are not deteriorating significantly. This is leading to some minor dovish repricing and weighing on the British pound.
The probability for a rate hike in December fell to 78% from 89% before the CPI release.
